answers_by_date.basis: Constitution art. 14 (every inhabitant may 'profesar libremente su culto'), art. 20 (foreigners 'ejercer libremente su culto') and art. 75 inc. 22 (ICCPR, ACHR with constitutional rank) were in force from the 1994 reform. Ley 22.439 contained nothing on religion. The CERD 2001 observations record xenophobic attitudes but no breach of migrants' religious freedom; practice evidence for this right is thin.

Same constitutional provisions. Ley 25.871 took effect on 21 Jan 2004 and added arts. 5, 6, 13 (religion as a prohibited ground) and 14(c) (valuing immigrants' religious expressions). We found no documented breach. CERD 2004 does not raise religious freedom for migrants.

Same provisions. Ley 26.202 approved the ICRMW (art. 12), which Argentina ratified on 23 Feb 2007; we could not open the law. We found no documented breach. The CMW 2011 observations raise discrimination concerns but not religious freedom.
No change to the provisions. We found no documented restriction on migrants' religious practice. Evidence on this specific right is thin.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

answers.sourcing_note: InfoLEG shows that the constitutional text has been unchanged since 1994, and we read both the original and the updated text of Ley 25.871. We could not open Ley 26.202. Practice evidence specific to religious freedom is essentially absent for every period.
answers.notes: The answer rests on the Constitution: arts. 14 and 20 are directly applicable, and art. 75 inc. 22 gives the listed treaties constitutional rank. The statutory additions (2004, 2007) reinforce the protection; they do not create it. The implementation ratings carry the 2020 rating back because no breach is documented. They are not based on positive evidence.

answers_by_date.basis: The regime was Ley 22.439, which mandated differential treatment by migration status. Art. 30 barred irregular migrants from work; art. 32 barred renting housing to them; art. 102 limited secondary and higher education to permanent or temporary residents; arts. 103-104 obliged hospitals and officials to report irregular migrants. Ley 23.592 and Constitution art. 16 prohibit discrimination on nationality, not on migration status. CERD 2001 recorded xenophobia and costly, bureaucratic regularisation for undocumented neighbouring-country migrants.

Ley 25.871 took effect on 21 Jan 2004 and repealed Ley 22.439. Its arts. 6-8 secure equal access and education and health 'cualquiera sea su situación migratoria', and art. 13 defines discrimination. CERD 2004 noted that implementing measures were still lacking and that INADI's budget had been severely reduced.

Same provisions. The regulating Decreto 616/2010 came only in May 2010. Over 2006-2010 the Patria Grande programme regularised large numbers of migrants. The CMW 2011 observations still report discrimination against migrant children at school, xenophobic statements by politicians, and media linking migrants to crime.
Same provisions, now regulated by Decreto 616/2010. INADI investigated complaints (CMW 2011). The CMW's 2019 concerns about DNU 70/2017 and provincial health restrictions concern 2017 onwards.

answers.sourcing_note: We read the original and updated texts of Ley 25.871, Ley 22.439 and Ley 23.592. We did not read Decreto 616/2010. The UN treaty-body observations give practice evidence for 2001, 2004 and 2011; there is no source specifically for around 2015.
answers.notes: The 2000 'No' is a judgement call. Ley 23.592 art. 1 (1988) already listed 'nacionalidad' as a ground, as Ley 25.871 art. 13 later did. Read the way the Colombia example reads national origin, it could support a 'Yes'. However, Ley 22.439 in force in 2000 expressly required exclusion and reporting of irregular migrants, so no general prohibition of discrimination by migration status existed until Ley 25.871 arts. 6-8 (21 Jan 2004). The 2020 citation's own basis for status-based protection is arts. 6-8.
